scenario.figure_or_table: Fig. 4 and Table I (steady-state 2D vs 3D thermal profiles; text on PDF pages 3-4)
scenario.description: Steady-state HotSpot v7.0 comparison of the MemPool 2D SoC against the MemPool-3D SoC in a memory-on-logic (MoL) F2F wafer-to-wafer hybrid-bonded stack with 1 MiB L1 SPM. The 3D stack has a 100 um memory die, a 2.85 um BEOL layer and a 5 um thinned logic die in a flip-chip package with heat spreader, heatsink, C4 bumps, substrate, solder balls and PCB. Paper-reported Tmax above ambient is 46 C for 2D, 55 C for the 3D memory die and 57 C for the 3D logic die.
scenario.architecture: MemPool 256-core 32-bit RISC-V many-core cluster with shared L1 scratchpad memory (64 tiles, 4 cores per tile, 16 KiB SPM blocks, 2 KiB I$). 3D version partitions each tile into a memory die (I$ and SPM) and a logic die (Snitch cores) in a 28 nm commercial technology. 3D die size is 3.95 x 3.95 mm; 2D footprint is 4.8 x 4.8 mm.
scenario.workload: Full workload at the 2D-SOC TDP baseline of 40 W. The 3D power is 0.913x of 2D because of fewer buffers, giving a power density 1.37x higher. No block-level floorplan coordinates or per-block powers are published in this paper; the floorplan is referenced to [38].
scenario.operating_point: Ambient 27 C, temperatures reported above ambient; heatsink-to-ambient Rconv 0.17 K/W; PCB-side natural convection 50 K/W; 7 W/m-K 100 um TIM; Tmax 2D 46 C, 3D memory die 55 C, 3D logic die 57 C.

original_setup.solver: HotSpot v7.0 steady-state thermal model (block/grid RC network solved by finite differences), described as validated against ANSYS and a thermal test chip. Ambient is 27 C and temperatures are reported above ambient.
original_setup.optimizer: None. The paper compares fixed configurations (2D vs 3D MoL/LoM, SPM capacities of 1 to 8 MiB, tile activity patterns P1 to P4) and runs no optimization algorithm.
original_setup.controller: None. No runtime thermal controller is used. DTM techniques are only mentioned in the introduction.
original_setup.benchmark: MemPool 256-core RISC-V SoC (64 tiles, 4 cores per tile) at a 40 W TDP for the 2D baseline under full workload. Selected scenario: 1 MiB L1 SPM, 2D vs 3D memory-on-logic (F2F hybrid-bonded) with the full package of Table I. Per-block floorplan coordinates and powers are not published in this paper.

thermal_observable.location: Hotspot in the logic die of the MemPool-3D SoC (memory-on-logic, 1 MiB SPM). Reported alongside 55 C in the memory die and 46 C for the 2D SoC.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum on-chip temperature (Tmax) from steady-state HotSpot, reported relative to a 27 C ambient. Values are read from the Fig. 4 labels and text, not tabulated.

physical_mismatches.reason: The scenario is a 3D face-to-face wafer-bonded memory-on-logic stack with a 2.85 um BEOL layer, a 100 um memory die and a 5 um thinned logic die. The bundled Studio model is presumably a planar 2D die and cannot represent two stacked tiers, the F2F bonding layer or inter-die coupling.

The full package is part of the result: 100 um TIM at 7 W/m-K, 5.92 mm heat spreader, 7.9 mm heatsink at Rconv 0.17 K/W, C4 bumps, substrate, solder balls, underfill and a 15x15 mm PCB with 50 K/W natural convection. A generic Studio cooling model likely does not reproduce this stack or the two-sided heat path.

Silicon thermal conductivity is size-dependent (140 W/m-K for 100 um, 100 W/m-K for the 5 um logic die). Thinning-induced ballistic phonon effects drive the logic-die hotspot, and a bulk-silicon Studio material would miss this.

The paper gives no block-level floorplan coordinates or per-block powers. Only die and tile sizes, a power-breakdown pie chart, a 40 W 2D TDP and a 0.913x 3D power scaling are given, and the floorplan is referenced to [38], which is not in the packet. A faithful 2D block-level Studio input cannot be built without inventing data.
The paper's solver is HotSpot with a specific block/grid RC model and uniform power per block. Studio's solver and meshing differ, so the 55 C and 57 C Tmax values cannot be assumed to match.

The paper contains no optimizer, controller, transient or reliability analysis in the selected scenario, so Studio features for those cannot be compared. The tile activity patterns and the SPM capacity and MOL/LOM sweeps are separate scenarios.

methods.note: The paper does state a steady-state HotSpot v7.0 block/grid RC solver, 27 C ambient and uniform power per block (PDF pp. 3-4). However, the extraction labels the experiment kind custom_2d_steady and sets steady_2d_relevant=false for a scenario that its own mismatches call an essential 3D F2F memory-on-logic stack. That stack has a 5 um thinned logic die, size-dependent silicon kth and a two-sided package heat path. Calling this a 2D reproduction is contradicted by the extraction itself.

code.note: The packet assets list is empty. The only link is the generic HotSpot GitHub URL from ref [45] on PDF p. 9. It is a bare URL and not a pinned asset, and it holds no MemPool floorplan, power or config files. The paper gives no code or data-availability statement. No code evidence exists.

parameters.note: The Table I layer sizes, thicknesses and kth, the Rconv values of 0.17 and 50 K/W, the 40 W 2D TDP, the 0.913x power scaling and the 1.37x density are supported by page text (PDF pp. 3-4). Decisive parameters are still missing or inferred. The SPM capacity (1 MiB) for Fig. 4 and the 'full workload' label are inferred, not stated. No absolute 3D power is given. HotSpot grid resolution and boundary settings are absent. The footprint scale is 0.665 in the text and 0.667 in Fig. 9. Table I's 2.85 um 'BEOL stack' is conflated with the 'F2F via layer of thickness 2.85 um' on p. 2.

data.note: No per-block power exists for any floorplan block in the same scenario. The Fig. 3 pie percentages (11/27/10/13/39) cannot be mapped to cores, I$, SPM, interconnects or others from garbled pdftotext. assessment.summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable (decision: not_2d_applicable, simulation_allowed false, comparison_valid false). Studio did not run; simulation status is 'skipped' because the custom experiment has no floorplan blocks and no power_w object, so there is no Studio result and no transient trace. The scenario is the paper's steady-state HotSpot comparison of a 1 MiB MemPool 2D SoC against a 3D face-to-face memory-on-logic stack, with reported Tmax above a 27 C ambient of 46 C (2D), 55 C (3D memory die) and 57 C (3D logic die). Because nothing ran, no Studio temperature can be compared with the 57 C logic-die observable or the other paper values, and no agreement or disagreement can be claimed. Essential physical mismatches would also block a numerical comparison even if a run were forced: a two-tier stacked geometry cannot be represented by a planar 2D die, the full package and two-sided heat path (TIM, spreader, heatsink at 0.17 K/W, substrate, PCB at 50 K/W) is not reproduced, size-dependent silicon conductivity (100 W/m-K for the 5 um logic die) is not captured, and no block-level floorplan or per-block power is published. The extracted evidence is only a record of the paper's stated parameters; it does not constitute a replication. Qualitatively, the paper reports that the 3D stack runs hotter than 2D, driven by roughly 1.37x higher power density, but this is the paper's claim and has not been tested here. The input and scientific gates failed, evidence locators and linked assets are unpinned, and adversarial and independent reviews are unresolved, so the final verdict stays at no valid comparison and no exact replication is claimed.
